A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BadScientist study. Their complete main texts, four tables, three figures, equations, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of generated papers and mitigation strategies in Tables 1–4, plus synthetic review-aggregation experiments in Appendix A.2 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and synthetic experiments. The absence of genuine experiments inside the fabricated manuscripts does not negate the paper's own evaluation results.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 revises the stated ReD/DetOnly detection objective from AI-generated content to fabricated or unsupported content, replacing NON-FABRICATED/AI-FABRICATED outputs with SUPPORTED/FABRICATION-RISK. This changes the mitigation specification; the generator and reviewer ensemble remain unchanged. Revised implementation or reruns are not documented.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same generated-paper coverage across 25 seed topics, ICLR 2025 submissions, the 50-real/50-generated mitigation dataset, and synthetic review scenarios. No additional population or scenario is tested following the detector reframing.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain o3, o4-mini, and GPT-4.1; baseline reviewing versus ReD in Table 3; and Random Guess, ReD, and DetOnly in Table 4. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sampling procedures, model configurations, metrics, the 200-paper calibration set, and thresholds of 7 and 6.667 remain unchanged. The new Evaluation Protocol paragraph consolidates the existing four generations per seed and fixed reviewer setup.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the strategy comparisons, score-distribution analysis, concern–acceptance analysis, mitigation evaluations, and Appendix A.2 sensitivity analyses for reviewer count and calibration size. No additional ablation or robustness evidence appears.

E5.justification: Four stochastic generations per seed were already documented across Sections 3.2 and 4.1. Appendix A.2 retains the same bootstrap analysis and Figure 3 uncertainty displays; v2 introduces no additional runs or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4 and the plotted results in Figures 2–3 are unchanged. Examples include 82.0% acceptance for TooGoodGains at the probability-consistency threshold and o3 detector accuracies of 67.0% for ReD and 57.0% for DetOnly.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, sampling derivation, concentration bounds, corollaries, calibration propositions, proof sketches, and Bayesian formulas are retained. Appendix A differs only in presentation and the wording 'multi-agent' versus 'agentic'.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: fabricated papers can receive high acceptance rates, integrity concerns conflict with recommendations, and the tested mitigations provide limited protection.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes legitimate presentation polish and AI-assisted writing from fabrication, explains the lightweight ensemble choice, and identifies richer reviewer architectures as future extensions. Ethical Considerations adds specific discussion of stylistic bias, neurodivergent researchers, reviewer workload, non-accusatory triage, and longitudinal threshold governance.

D1.justification: The added protocol summary repeats previously supplied generation counts, models, rubric, default uniform weights, and thresholds. Implementation information, the project-page disclosure, and public versus restricted artifact-release arrangements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to research agents, automated peer review, and integrity attacks. The added ensemble rationale does not introduce a new prior-work comparison or novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanations and ethics paragraphs, standardizes several heading capitalizations, changes some agent terminology, and adds a HUMAIN affiliation. The section sequence and most prose remain intact; a few new typographical errors also appear.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged, and Tables 1–2 and Figure 2 are rearranged together on PDF page 7. Other content reflows and page-number footers disappear. The figures, table structures, and captions otherwise retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves conceptual clarity by distinguishing legitimate writing assistance and polish from fabrication, and adds concrete applicability limits and deployment safeguards. These are useful refinements to the interpretation of unchanged evidence. The revised mitigation specification receives no new validation, and minor proofreading defects remain, so the overall gain is limited.
